newsitem.title: USA: Alaska governor leads Sakhalin oil trade mission.
newsitem.headline: Alaska governor leads Sakhalin oil trade mission.

text.p: Alaska Gov. Tony Knowles will lead a delegation of more than 40 business representatives and government officials to the Russian Far East island of Sakhalin this weekend to explore possible joint ventures in oil and gas development.

"Alaskans are world leaders in cold weather oil and gas development and our expertise is being sought in the Russian Far East," Knowles said in a news release issued on Thursday. "This trade mission is designed to open important doors for Alaska companies and provide jobs for Alaskans."
The trip is scheduled to begin on Saturday and officials are scheduled to return on Wednesday, Knowles said.
Accompanying the Democratic governor will be leaders of Alaska's Republican-controlled state legislature and representatives from Exxon, Texaco, Tesoro Alaska Petroleum Co.
Anchorage-based Reeve Aleutian Airways will use the trade mission to inaugurate regular service to Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, Knowles said.
Sakhalin is the site of four major oil and gas projects involving international oil companies, including Exxon, Mobil, Texaco and Marathon Oil, the governor said.

This will be his second official mission to Sakhalin. He traveled to the island two years ago to deliver medical supplies to help residents cope with a major earthquake on the northern part of the island.
